title: Lions and Contamination: Trees and General Graphs
summary: This paper investigates a special variant of a pursuit-evasion game called lions and contamination. In a graph where all vertices are initially contaminated, a set of lions traverses the graph, clearing the contamination from every vertex they visit. However, the contamination simultaneously spreads to any adjacent vertex not occupied by a lion. We analyze the relationships among the lion number $\mathcal{L}(G)$, monotone lion number $\mathcal{L}^m(G)$, and the graph's pathwidth $\operatorname{pw}(G)$.
